thread:
anne-docs: Quick heads-up 14 I opened a docs PR with guidance on audit-log sampling, export behavior under legal hold, and short SDK/curl snippets. Link: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/5901

mike-security: Thanks. Two immediate asks: (1) scrub wording that implies indefinite storage (avoid 'we may keep' or 'indefinitely'), (2) clearly call out that sampled queries are for operational triage and not a substitute for full exports during legal investigations.

anne-docs: Got it. Current draft sentence: 'By default logs are retained for 90 days. Exports made for compliance reasons may be retained longer under legal hold.' Is that acceptable for SOC2 docs?

mike-security: Slight tweak: 'Customer audit logs are retained for 90 days by default. Legal holds or regulatory obligations can extend retention; access controls are enforced on exported data.' That removes first-person phrasing. :+1:

pratyusha-eng: I pushed three short examples we can drop into the PR: python, TS, curl. Python sampling example: ```python
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
# request ~1% sample across a date range for quick triage
resp = client.query_events(sample=0.01, start='2025-02-01', end='2025-03-03')
print(resp['total'])
```

anne-docs: Perfect. Can you make the TS example non-blocking (i.e., show promise/async usage) and a one-liner curl for ops?

pratyusha-eng: TS example: ```ts
import { AuditClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const c = new AuditClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
const { total } = await c.queryEvents({ sample: 0.01, start: '2025-02-01', end: '2025-03-03' })
console.log(total)
```

pratyusha-eng: Curl: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/query \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sample":0.01, "start":"2025-02-01", "end":"2025-03-03"}'
```

jordan-legal: A couple legal points: (1) use phrase 'as required by law or contractual obligations' instead of 'may be retained longer', (2) add a legal-hold contact (legal@redwood.com) and short note that example IDs in docs are pseudonymized.

anne-docs: Will add both. Thinking of a tiny pseudonymization snippet to demonstrate best practice; want to keep it short and non-opinionated.

mike-security: Good idea. Show a one-line transform that replaces user_id with a SHA256 prefix, like `user_id: sha256:...`. Keep it illustrative, not production-ready.

pratyusha-eng: Added the pseudonymized JSON example for the doc: ```json
{
  "user_id": "sha256:3f2a9b...",
  "event": "model.generate",
  "ts": "2025-03-01T12:00:00Z"
}
```

lina-ml: Small content suggestion: add a callout about sampling bias 14 sampled datasets can under-represent rare anomalies. Recommend full exports prior to any formal compliance investigation. Link to monitoring playbook in ops docs.

anne-docs: Added the callout and playbook link. Also added a short sentence explaining difference between 'sample' (statistical sample) and 'export' (complete dump).

mike-security: LGTM overall. I left one inline wording suggestion (changing 'exports made for compliance reasons' to 'exports created to satisfy regulatory or contractual obligations'). I'll push that suggestion to PR.

anne-docs: Thanks! Plan to merge on Wednesday after security + legal ack. @doc-bot would you auto-label merged PRs with 'security-reviewed'?

doc-bot: PR updated: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/5901/files 14 requested reviewers: @mike-security @jordan-legal @pratyusha-eng

anne-docs: Thanks everyone. Final checklist: update wording per mike, add legal-hold contact, ensure snippets are present (py/ts/curl), add pseudonymization example, include monitoring playbook link. Will merge once security signs off.
